name: Datadog
description: Protects against destructive Datadog CLI/API operations like deleting monitors and dashboards.

destructive_patterns.name: datadog-ci-monitors-delete
destructive_patterns.description: datadog-ci monitors delete removes a Datadog monitor.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a Datadog monitor stops all alerting for that check. You will no \ longer be notified if the monitored condition occurs, potentially missing \ critical production issues.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - datadog-ci monitors get <id>: Review the monitor configuration first \ - Mute the monitor temporarily instead of deleting \ - Export monitor JSON configuration as backup before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: datadog-ci-dashboards-delete
destructive_patterns.description: datadog-ci dashboards delete removes a Datadog dashboard.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a dashboard removes all widgets, queries, and layout configuration. \ Team members relying on this dashboard for visibility will lose access \ immediately.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - datadog-ci dashboards get <id>: Export dashboard JSON first \ - Clone the dashboard before making changes \ - Use Terraform or Pulumi for version-controlled dashboard definitions

destructive_patterns.name: datadog-api-delete
destructive_patterns.description: Datadog API DELETE calls remove monitors/dashboards/synthetics.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Direct API DELETE calls permanently remove Datadog resources without \ confirmation prompts. Monitors, dashboards, and synthetic tests are deleted \ immediately.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - GET the resource first to verify the ID and export configuration \ - Use datadog-ci CLI which provides better feedback \ - Use Terraform/Pulumi for auditable, reversible infrastructure changes

destructive_patterns.name: terraform-datadog-destroy
destructive_patterns.description: terraform destroy targeting Datadog resources removes monitoring infrastructure.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Terraform destroy removes Datadog monitors, dashboards, and other resources \ defined in your configuration. While Terraform tracks state, the actual \ monitoring resources are deleted immediately from Datadog.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - terraform plan -destroy -target=... to preview deletions \ - terraform state rm to stop managing without deleting \ - Remove from Terraform config and apply instead of destroy
